title: Exact completed extension and sections adjunction at a point
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\ge1$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and use its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $(R,B)$ be either $(A_{E,n},(A_{E,n})_s)$, where $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, or $(\mathcal O_E,\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,s})$, using the constant and completed coefficient sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. For an arbitrary $R$-module $M$, let $\underline M$ be its constant module sheaf [def-sf-site-constant-module-functor] and define $L_RM=B\otimes_{\underline R}\underline M$ by sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Then $L_R:\operatorname{Mod}(R)\to\operatorname{Mod}(B)$ and $\Gamma_s:F\mapsto F(s)$ are exact, and the constant-value map $R\to\Gamma_s B$ is an isomorphism of rings. There is a natural adjunction
$$\operatorname{Hom}_B(L_RM,F)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,\Gamma_s F)$$
for all $M$ and all $B$-module sheaves $F$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. It sends $h$ to $m\mapsto h_s(1\otimes m)$; the inverse sends $t:M\to F(s)$ to the sheaf map whose local rule over $U$ is $b\otimes m\mapsto b\,t(m)|_U$. Applied termwise to complexes, these rules commute with the differentials and identify chain maps and chain homotopies. No constructibility or finite-generation hypothesis is imposed on $M$ or $F$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pod-integral-point-coefficient-adjunction] to the given finite-field datum and coefficient extension. It supplies the exact integral extension functor with exactly the published objects and maps, exact integral sections, the normalized ordinary adjunction, and both integral and finite constant-value bijections. For finite coefficients write n=m+1 using n>=1 to match its finite index. The remaining work is finite extension and the componentwise complex and homotopy equivalences.

proof.text: Construct the Hom equivalence from constant module presheaves to a module presheaf by evaluation at the final object. Its inverse restricts a final-object section along the unique structure map to each object; naturality and finality prove the inverse identities. Compose with the module sheafification Hom equivalence [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] for the constant-module construction [def-sf-site-constant-module-functor]. Compose the resulting adjunction with the proved sheafified tensor/restriction adjunction used in [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-coefficient-ordinary-adjunction]. Scalar restriction followed by point sections agrees with the published sections functor. This gives the adjunction for the prescribed extension objects and maps. Its forward rule is evaluation on 1 tensor m. For the inverse rule, naturality gives the formula on 1 tensor m over every object and B-linearity gives the formula on b tensor m.

source.place: Tags 03CY, 03EI and 03EK; universal properties and exact module sheafification

proof.text: Constant module presheaves preserve finite limits and finite colimits objectwise. Exact module sheafification [lem-weil-pbc-site-r-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact] therefore makes the published constant module functor exact. At finite level the coefficient map is the identity of the constant ring sheaf. Restriction along that identity has its tautological natural isomorphism to the identity functor. Transport the tensor adjunction of step 2 through this isomorphism; uniqueness of left adjoints identifies its tensor functor with the identity. Hence finite extension, the composite of constant modules and that tensor functor, is exact.

source.place: Tags 03CY, 03EI and 03EK; universal properties and exact module sheafification

proof.text: The algebraic closure in the finite-field datum is algebraically closed. Apply the arbitrary-module exact sections clause of [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact] to the finite coefficient sheaf. Compose its final-object evaluation with restriction along the constant-value scalar map. Restriction preserves finite limits and colimits, giving the required exact finite sections functor.

proof.text: For either exact ordinary adjunction, use Adjunction.mapHomologicalComplex from the source library to obtain the equivalence on unbounded cochain maps. Its degree-i component is definitionally the ordinary Hom equivalence. Given an actual homotopy H, apply the ordinary Hom equivalence to H.hom i j in every pair of degrees. Additivity sends sums to sums, and its two naturality laws carry the two differential composites to the corresponding composites. Thus the homotopy equation and the off-shape zero condition hold. The inverse ordinary Hom equivalence gives the inverse homotopy construction, and the inverse identities hold componentwise. Package these witnesses together with exactness, the constant-value bijection, and the ordinary adjunction into ExactExtensionSections. No boundedness or finiteness assumption enters.

At finite level the multiplication map b(x)x -> bx is an isomorphism. Integrally O_E is a PID, hence Noetherian, and completed-constant-sheaf-reduction with T=s, A=O_E, I=(varpi) gives flatness of exactly the inverse-limit sheaf of def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients (same site and same constant sheaf). S3: point sections on the small site are exact for every ring sheaf, since k=Fbar_q is algebraically closed; restricting scalars to R keeps exactness. S4: finite level uses finite quotients plus finite-constant-sections at X=V=s, a ring isomorphism normalized on constants. Its 'canonical' isomorphism is the reduction map (BS 6.8.2(1) proof: Map_cont(S,O_E)=lim Map_cont(S,O_E/varpi^n)), so it is compatible with constants and R->B(s) is a ring isomorphism. S5: checked the adjunction construction line by line. The map g_t is R_-linear by uniqueness of the extended action; (b,x)->b g_t(x) is balanced; both inverse checks hold via sheafification uniqueness and B-linearity; naturality is explicit. S6: chain maps and homotopies are identified degree by degree with only adjacent terms, so unbounded complexes are fine. Edge cases checked: M=0, F=0, n=1, infinite M, F(s)=0 (no conservativity is claimed).
